sub: Connection and background to Syrian Civil War

slides.title: From Iraq War to Syrian Civil War
slides.cap: Historical overview: From Iraq War to Syrian Civil War
slides.body:
The Iraq War destabilized the region and strengthened jihadist networks, while the Arab Spring inspired protests against authoritarian governments. Syria's security forces violently suppressed demonstrations against Bashar al-Assad, turning an uprising into civil war.

Syrians fought over dictatorship, revolution, territory, communal survival, and the country's political future, while Russia, Iran, Turkey, the United States, Israel, and armed groups pursued competing interests.

The Daraa crackdown transformed demands for reform into a nationwide challenge to authoritarian rule. Militarization then fragmented the uprising among local rebels, Islamists, Kurdish forces, and jihadists, while foreign intervention gave the conflict several overlapping regional and international fronts.

stats.lbl: Syrians fought over dictatorship, revolution, territory, communal survival, and the country's political future, while Russia, Iran, Turkey, the United States, Israel, and armed groups pursued competing interests.

markers.label: Daraa
markers.description: Protests and regime violence in Daraa helped ignite the national uprising.

slides.title: Daraa Protests and Crackdown
slides.cap: Historical overview: Daraa Protests and Crackdown
slides.body:
Protests spread after the arrest and abuse of schoolchildren in Daraa. Security forces used lethal force, fueling nationwide demonstrations and armed resistance.

The arrest and torture of schoolchildren made local corruption and police abuse a national symbol. Funeral protests, lethal shootings, and failed concessions spread mobilization beyond Daraa and encouraged defections from a security apparatus ordered to suppress civilians.

markers.label: Aleppo
markers.description: Years of urban warfare made Aleppo one of the war's defining battles.

slides.title: Battle of Aleppo
slides.body:
Rebel forces entered Aleppo, beginning years of urban warfare. Government forces, backed by Russia and Iran-aligned forces, recaptured the eastern districts in December 2016.

Control of Syria's largest city divided between rebel east and government west, producing siege, bombardment, and immense displacement. The government's 2016 victory, enabled by Russian airpower and Iran-aligned ground forces, ended the opposition's best chance to hold a major urban capital.

markers.label: Eastern Ghouta
markers.description: Rockets carrying sarin struck opposition-held suburbs near Damascus.

markers.label: Damascus
markers.description: The attack occurred on the capital's doorstep and triggered global outrage.

slides.title: Ghouta Chemical Attack
slides.body:
Rockets carrying sarin struck opposition-held areas near Damascus, killing large numbers of civilians. Syria later agreed to surrender its declared chemical arsenal under an international deal.

The sarin attack brought the war to the edge of direct US intervention after President Obama's chemical-weapons warning. The resulting US-Russian agreement removed much of Syria's declared arsenal but left Assad in power and failed to prevent later chemical attacks.

markers.label: Raqqa
markers.description: Raqqa became ISIS's de facto Syrian capital.

markers.label: Mosul
markers.description: ISIS's Iraq-Syria expansion made the war regional.

slides.title: Rise of ISIS
slides.body:
ISIS proclaimed a caliphate across parts of Syria and Iraq. A US-led coalition began airstrikes and supported local partners, especially the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces.

ISIS erased parts of the Iraq-Syria border, captured oil fields and cities, and imposed mass violence under its caliphate. Fighting it redirected Western policy toward counterterrorism, strengthened Kurdish-led forces, and complicated the original contest between Assad and the rebellion.

markers.label: Hmeimim airbase
markers.description: Russian air power from Hmeimim helped rescue Assad's position.

markers.label: Latakia
markers.description: Russia anchored its Syrian intervention on the Mediterranean coast.

slides.title: Russian Military Intervention
slides.body:
Russia intervened directly with air power in support of Assad, helping reverse rebel gains and preserve the government.

Russian aircraft and advisers prevented further government collapse and targeted a broad range of opposition forces as well as ISIS. The intervention restored Assad's strategic initiative and shifted diplomacy away from a negotiated transition toward arrangements shaped by Moscow, Tehran, and Ankara.

markers.label: Baghuz
markers.description: The Syrian Democratic Forces captured ISIS's last territorial enclave here.

markers.label: Euphrates Valley
markers.description: ISIS's final territorial fight unfolded along the Euphrates.

slides.title: Fall of Baghuz
slides.body:
The Syrian Democratic Forces captured ISIS's last major territorial enclave at Baghuz, ending the group's territorial caliphate while its insurgency continued.

The capture of Baghuz ended ISIS control of a territorial state but not its clandestine network. Thousands of detainees and families entered prisons and camps in northeastern Syria, creating an unresolved security and humanitarian burden for Kurdish-led authorities.

markers.label: Damascus
markers.description: The fall of Damascus ended Assad family rule in the main civil-war phase.

markers.label: Aleppo-Hama-Homs axis
markers.description: A rapid opposition offensive moved through Syria's western spine.

slides.title: Fall of Assad
slides.body:
A rapid opposition offensive captured Aleppo, Hama, Homs, and Damascus. Bashar al-Assad fled to Russia, ending his family's rule and the principal civil-war phase.

The rapid offensive exposed how dependent the regime had become on exhausted foreign-backed military structures. Assad's flight ended dynastic rule, but the victory left a fragmented country containing armed factions, foreign troops, displaced populations, and unresolved Kurdish and regional questions.

title: Conflict Summary: Syrian Civil War
sub: Final summary of Syrian Civil War

markers.label: Damascus
markers.description: The regime's collapse did not end Syria's fragmentation or humanitarian crisis.

markers.label: Northern Syria
markers.description: Kurdish, Turkish-backed, jihadist, and post-regime forces remained central to the aftermath.

slides.title: Conflict Summary: Syrian Civil War
slides.cap: Historical overview: Conflict Summary: Syrian Civil War
slides.body:
Opposition forces overthrew Assad in December 2024 after nearly fourteen years of war. Syria remained fractured and violent during the transition, with foreign troops, ISIS cells, communal tensions, and unresolved Kurdish and regional disputes continuing beyond the civil war's principal phase.

Taken as a whole, Syrian Civil War shows how battlefield achievements can alter the balance of power without necessarily producing a durable political settlement. The outcome must therefore be judged by the security conditions it created, the threats that survived, the human cost, and whether later leaders learned from the campaign.
